questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake. It is attached to the ____ valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line is attached to relay valves. These valves allow the trailer brakes to be applied quickly.

questions.question: More than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by:
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your truck. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: When an air supply control is in the "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is in the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes are applied.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest loaded trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Keeping cargo low lowers the vehicle's center of gravity. This helps prevent rollovers when turning.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need extra space on the road because they:

options.text: Drive more slowly than other commercial motor vehicles.
Are heavier than other commercial motor vehicles.
Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop. You must manage space carefully when operating a combination vehicle.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before each trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It may release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is by:

options.text: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see if your trailer is skidding or jackknifing. This lets you spot problems early.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: What do you test by placing the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. Pull out the trailer air supply control or put it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Drivers must use caution when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When you take a turn too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you take a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To avoid rollovers, drive slowly on ramps and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when pulling trailers.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, what following distance should you maintain for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, what should the driver do?

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Can straighten the trailer with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the trailer wheels regain grip on the road. Do not use the trailer hand brake because braking caused the wheels to lock in the first place.

questions.question: Which action will NOT help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep cargo weight as close to the ground as possible when loading. Also drive slowly around turns. Driving on the shoulder does not prevent rollovers.

questions.question: How can you check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To see if an older vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What is one benefit of keeping cargo centered on a rig?
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading increases rollover risk. Keep cargo centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Driving combination vehicles usually requires ____ skill than driving single vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require higher driving skill to operate safely.
